transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I guess I’m here because... honestly, for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It's just constant. Like, little billing errors will suddenly show up at work—I do posting and billing, and we use this really outdated software, honestly it's from like ten years ago and the screen constantly freezes when I'm trying to input the daily codes. I keep telling my supervisor we need an IT upgrade, but he just talks about the quarterly budget. 

Anyway, the errors keep happening, and then someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me. Like last Sunday, Brenda completely walked past me during coffee hour. She usually always stops to chat about her garden, she grows those huge heirloom tomatoes and brings them in little baskets, but she just looked right past me and walked away. But no matter what records anyone pulls up, I know it all ties back to his family doing this. They are behind it. 

Oh, by the way, the signage in your parking garage is really hard to read. I ended up parking on the completely wrong level and almost dropped my keys down the grate trying to find the elevator. It's very poorly lit down there. What were we talking about? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, it's just... nobody is looking at the connections with his family.
Have you been experiencing any significant periods where your mood has been extremely high or extremely low, beyond just feeling stressed about these family issues?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm stressed, sure, but I'm not... I don't get super depressed or bouncing off the walls or anything. I'm just a normal person trying to deal with all this. 

Speaking of normal, though, you wouldn't believe what they charge for a regular black coffee in your lobby downstairs. I stopped to get one because I had a little extra time after the whole parking garage debacle, and it was almost four dollars! For just plain coffee! I usually bring my own in a thermos. My husband bought me this really nice silver thermos for our anniversary a couple years ago, it keeps things hot until at least two in the afternoon. But I left it on the kitchen counter this morning because I was rushing to find my good coat. The zipper on my everyday jacket got completely stuck yesterday. I swear they don't make zippers like they used to. Everything is just cheap plastic now, you know? It just snaps right off in your hand if you pull too hard. 

But... wait, what did you ask me? Oh, my mood. No, my mood is fine, honestly. It's just the stress of knowing what his family is up to and nobody listening to me about it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice?

Voices? No, no, I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. I mean, the only voices I hear are the ones I'm actually supposed to hear. Though, honestly, sometimes I wish I couldn't hear my coworker, Linda. She sits in the space right next to mine—well, it's not even a real cubicle, it's just one of those low frosted-glass partitions they put up when they remodeled the billing department back in 2018. Management said it was supposed to encourage open communication, but really it just means I have to hear every single time she crunches on her ice. 

She goes to the breakroom every day at 1:15 and fills her cup with that crushed ice, the really good kind, you know? Like the kind they have at Sonic? But then she just sits there and chomps on it all afternoon while she's sorting the invoices. I actually brought in a pair of headphones, the big over-the-ear ones my niece bought me for Christmas, but they give me a terrible headache if I wear them for more than an hour. They squeeze right behind my ears. I think I might just have a wider head than most people. I always have trouble buying hats, too, especially those cute sun hats. They just pop right off the top of my head the second there's a breeze. 

But... wait, what were you asking me about Linda? Oh, or was it the office? I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought.
Have you ever considered that there might be any other explanation for the billing errors and Brenda's behavior, or are you absolutely certain that your husband's family is responsible?

No, there's no other explanation. I am absolutely certain. I know how it sounds, but I've been dealing with this for months. I just... I need people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. The billing errors at work, Brenda acting strange at church—it all ties back to them. No matter what records anyone pulls up, I just know it's them. 

Speaking of records, though, my husband and I were looking for our old tax returns the other day. We keep them in this heavy metal filing cabinet in the basement. It's one of those old olive-green ones, you know? The kind that weighs a ton and the drawers always stick? We got it at a garage sale years ago from this lovely older couple who were moving to Florida. They had this beautiful golden retriever that just wanted to lean against your legs the whole time we were loading the cabinet into the truck. I love dogs, but we can't have one because my husband is terribly allergic to dander. His eyes swell up like balloons. We tried having a fish once, a little betta fish named Barnaby, but it just wasn't the same. 

Anyway, the filing cabinet... the bottom drawer was completely jammed, and when my husband finally yanked it open, it scraped the linoleum floor. We just put down that new flooring last spring, too. It's supposed to look like distressed oak, but it's really just that click-together vinyl stuff. It's so much easier to clean than the old carpet we had down there, though. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the errors and Brenda. No, there's no other explanation. It's definitely his family behind it all.

I've noticed that while we are talking, you often shift your focus to other details like office supplies or furniture; do you often feel like your thoughts are jumping around or that you have trouble staying on track when you're trying to explain something?

No, I don't think my thoughts jump around at all. I actually think I'm very focused. You have to be incredibly focused in billing, you know? If you lose track for even a second, you could put a decimal in the wrong place. 

That actually happened to Dave, the guy who used to sit over by the main copy machine. He billed a patient four thousand dollars instead of forty, and the poor man called in absolutely screaming at our receptionist, Patty. Patty definitely didn't deserve that, she is just the sweetest lady. She brings in homemade blueberry muffins every other Friday for the whole office. She uses her grandmother's recipe, which has sour cream in the batter to keep them really moist. I tried making them at home for my husband once, but I was completely out of sour cream so I used plain Greek yogurt instead. They came out so incredibly dense, like little bricks. My husband wouldn't even eat them. He ended up crumbling them up and putting them out on the bird feeder in the backyard. 

We get a lot of blue jays back there. They're pretty, but they're so mean to the smaller birds. They just swoop in and scare all the little goldfinches away. I bought this special thistle seed just for the finches, but the blue jays just knock the feeder around until it spills everywhere. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about my thoughts. No, I don't have trouble staying on track. I just like to make sure I give you the whole picture so you understand exactly what I mean.
Have you ever had any major medical problems, or have you been taking any prescription medications, vitamins, or supplements on a regular basis?

Medical problems? No, no major medical problems. I'm perfectly healthy. And I don't take any prescription medications or anything like that. I did try taking a daily vitamin for a little while, one of those gummy ones? My sister-in-law swore by them. Well, not the sister-in-law who's messing with our accounts, the other one, Sarah. She lives out in Oregon and is always sending us these care packages full of natural, organic stuff. 

Last month she sent this huge glass jar of raw local honey. It was supposed to be really good for allergies, which I thought would be perfect for my husband, you know, with the dander issue I was telling you about earlier. But he absolutely refused to touch it because it had this weird, cloudy look to it. It crystallized at the bottom, too. I ended up putting it in my chamomile tea for a few weeks, but honestly, I just prefer regular white sugar. The little paper packets you get at diners? I always grab a few extra when we go to this diner down the street on Sunday mornings. They make the absolute best hash browns. They fry them on this massive flat-top grill so they get incredibly crispy on the edges but stay soft in the middle. I tried making them like that at home in my cast iron skillet, but they just sort of turned into a greasy mush... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask me what I eat for breakfast?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to take care of yourself, such as difficulty with personal hygiene or keeping your home tidy, over the past several months?

No, I haven't had any trouble like that. I still get up for work every single morning, handle all my billing clerk duties, keep the house going, and I even still spend plenty of time gardening and painting. Actually, I was just painting the trim in our guest bedroom last weekend. We decided to go with this color called Navajo White, though honestly, it just looks like a very pale yellow in the afternoon sun. I bought the paint at that little hardware store on Elm Street. The guy working the counter—I think his name tag said Gary—he was wearing this incredibly bright orange apron. It reminded me of those construction cones they put out on the highway. 

They've been doing roadwork on the interstate for what feels like ten years now. The traffic is just unbearable if you hit it past 3:30 PM. My husband got stuck in it for two hours last Tuesday when he was trying to pick up his suits from the dry cleaners. He was so frustrated he actually honked his horn, which he never does. He's usually such a patient driver, not like my brother, who just yells at every single car that cuts him off. He drives this huge red pickup truck that barely fits in our driveway when he comes over for Thanksgiving...

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, about taking care of myself and the house. No, the house is fine and I'm fine. The main trouble only really comes up when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing. Trying to get people to listen to the truth about them, that's the only thing that really drains me.
